mechanism: Separate the actual folded-paper diagonal cut (red) from one discarded-corner vertical ghost trace (blue), then pair these with alternating horizontalred and verticalblue edges of A inner square. Targets constructing a square hole partly from cut edges and partly from folded-corner/crease traces instead of reflecting the actual diagonalcut through both folds. The source diagonal remains slanted and the blue source remains dashed; those visible distinctions reject the false edge roles.
mathematical_solution: The horizontal then vertical half-fold leaves one quarter of the original square, and its clipped lower-left corner is the original sheet centre. In coordinates where the centre is(0,0), the removed triangle is{x>=0,y>=0,x+y<0.75}. Reflection across both axes produces{|x|+|y|<0.75}, one centraldiamond opening, with the original square outerboundary untouched. B alone has that outerboundary and diamondhole. A squarehole sides are horizontal/vertical and cannot arise by those axis-reflections of the true45degreecut; C has no centralhole, D no centralhole plus outercornercuts, E adds outercornercuts. Thus B is unique. The ghost trace is not an extra cut and must not be included in the opened hole.
